companies.credit_view: GDS remains a highly levered (5.5x reported net debt/LQA EBITDA, ~5.1x on LTM incl. finance leases; ~4.0x excluding them) but improving China hyperscale operator whose deleveraging has come from asset monetization (C-REIT, DayOne stake sales) rather than organic FCF. The near-term pressure point is the ~US$620M 2029 convertible put in March 2027, now current, against ~US$2.2B cash (more incl. time deposits) and demonstrated onshore bank access (RMB4.9B new/refinanced in Q2). The 2026 capex step-up to RMB10B (2x 2025) with 60/40 debt/equity funding will re-lever unless C-REIT injections recycle capital. Not rated by the big three; credit is driven by onshore bank relationships, recurring C-REIT recycling and convert-market access.

Moody's moved the outlook back to stable in Apr 2026, so ratings headroom depends on the quick-commerce losses narrowing and capex staying within the RMB380B plan; continued debt-funded capex with falling EBITDA would erode the net cash cushion.

The rating story hinges on whether shareholder returns are moderated while capex stays elevated; absent that, Tencent could move to net debt by 2027, though its core cash-generating franchise (operating cash inflow RMB52.7B/quarter) keeps leverage manageable.
